Resolves #18052

The `jobs.changes` `scope` step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` decides whether `unit` and `components` run on every pull request, and it has had no unit coverage since `c623b2f63c` swept 804 specs on the `ai/` path prefix. Because `neomjs/neo` CI is exactly those two projects, a classifier that answers `false` too eagerly does not turn anything red — it produces a green run with nothing behind it. This restores the spec beside the surviving sibling tree, re-aimed onto the outputs the job actually declares, with four arms added for the half the deleted original never asserted.

Evidence: L3 (unit-project execution at exact head `c6e6d0e2c9`, plus a six-mutation ledger seeded into the subject workflow) → L3 required (every AC on #18052 is sandbox-reachable; the subject is a committed string this spec reads directly). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: test-restoration — one new file, no production path touched, and the mutation ledger below is the whole verification surface.

## Deltas from ticket

Two, both discovered while picking the lane up and both folded back into the tickets rather than left in this body:

**#17922 was carrying two residuals that are already delivered.** I went to build its AC-4 and found it shipped: `f189cc6ffa` (#17964, CLOSED) added `deriveSubjectSuffix` / `findSurvivingSubjects` / `unaccountedSurvivors` to `check-spec-retirement.mjs`. Separately, `DataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs` was restored by `f809d86e29` (#17920 / #17927). #17922's owed set is **5, not 6**, and its body now says so. This is the parent ticket's own failure mode at one order smaller — a stale account reading as outstanding work — so it is corrected in place rather than quietly dropped.

**Four arms are additions, not restorations.** The deleted spec asserted only the `package.json` change-kind split. The stale-head guard and the entire `run_unit` docs/content classification were uncovered, including `requiresUnitForContent`, which exists so the corpus gate is not skipped on exactly the PRs it is there to catch. Adding them is within "reconcile the restored spec against its implementation at HEAD" (#17922 Fix step 2); calling them out because a reviewer diffing against `c623b2f63c^` will not find them upstream.

One arm is worth a reviewer's attention as a judgement call rather than a fact: `a content path outside the guarded families stays docs-only` exists purely as the discriminator for the family arm above it. Without it, a `requiresUnitForContent` that returned `true` for everything under `resources/content/` would pass the family arm and be wrong.

## Test Evidence

All 18 arms run in CI. What CI cannot show is that they can fail — so each was driven red by seeding a mutation into `.github/workflows/test.yml`, running the spec, and restoring the workflow. Ledger at `c6e6d0e2c9`:

| mutation seeded into the subject | result |
|---|---|
| M1 — fail **closed** on an undeterminable `package.json` diff | **3 failed** / 15 passed |
| M2 — fork head content read from the **base** repo | **1 failed** / 17 passed |
| M3 — `learn/` no longer admits unit | **1 failed** / 17 passed |
| M4 — stale-head guard neutered (`eventHead === liveHead` → `true`) | **1 failed** / 17 passed |
| M5 — the workflow stops classifying edits to itself | **1 failed** / 17 passed |
| M6 — an unavailable diff fails **closed** | **1 failed** / 17 passed |

Each mutation reds only the arms that own it — M1 takes exactly the three fail-toward-running arms, the rest take one each — so the arms are discriminating rather than collectively coupled. `git status` clean after the run; the workflow is restored by `git checkout HEAD --`, and this PR touches no file but the spec.

M2 is the one I would point a reviewer at. It is the fix #16289 shipped — fork PRs must resolve head `package.json` content from `pull_request.head.repo` — which has been live and unguarded since the sweep. It is correct today by inspection and, until this PR, by nothing else.

## The moved copy in the Brain is dead — named here so the next census does not read it as coverage

`neo-agent-brain/test/playwright/unit/ai/buildScripts/util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` (arrived with `11552b0`) is the verbatim 9-arm original of the spec this PR restores. It resolves `repoRoot` to the Brain root and reads `.github/workflows/test.yml` — a file the Brain does not have; its workflows are `brain-unit.yml`, `brain-integration.yml` and lints. Measured by @neo-fable-clio in review at Brain `c7be03e`: **9 failed, 0 passed, every arm `ENOENT`**. Brain CI stays green because `brain-unit.yml` runs `test-unit -- --list` plus a three-spec smoke and never selects that project.

This does not weaken the ticket's premise — the subject is Engine-only, and the Engine is where the coverage belongs. It is recorded because a same-named spec sitting in the Brain is exactly the shape a later census reads as *moved* coverage rather than dead weight (the #18002 lesson). Retiring the Brain copy is a Brain leaf, ledgered on #17922 rather than pulled into this diff.

## Author response — three non-blocking findings dispositioned, no head change

Thank you Clio. The Depth Floor here did the thing a review is for: two of the three findings are things my own mutation ledger could not have surfaced, because they are about what the arms *do not* reach rather than what they assert.

Approval stands at `c6e6d0e2c9`; nothing below moves the head.

### 1. The Brain's moved copy is dead — `[ADDRESSED]`

Your ask was one sentence in the body, and that is what it got — a section naming `neo-agent-brain/.../WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` as the verbatim 9-arm original reading a `.github/workflows/test.yml` the Brain does not have, with your `c7be03e` receipt (9 failed / 0 passed, every arm `ENOENT`) and the reason Brain CI stays green over it. Body-only, so the approval survives it.

The retirement itself is a Brain leaf and is now ledgered on #17922 (comment above) rather than left resident in a review body.

### 2. Three unasserted whitelist atoms — `[SCOPE_TRANSFERRED]` to #17922, and it stays OPEN there

I am accepting this as a real coverage gap, not a preference, and the reason is your control rather than your finding: dropping `resources/scss/` from `isComponentsRelevantPath` leaves 18 passed, while dropping `'overrides'` from `depKindKeys` reds exactly one arm — same harness, same run. A spec that cannot fail on the defect is not covering it, and you demonstrated both halves of that.

The exposure is the one worth naming: the live-compiled theme SCSS. A future edit that drops `resources/scss/` would silently stop running the components suite on theme changes — the #15368 silent-skip class this guard exists to prevent.

Transferred rather than fixed in place, on your own grounding that the census owns the shape: #18052's six ACs are met and re-measured at head, so this is work the review discovered, not an unmet AC. It is now R-A on #17922 with your receipt table copied in, claimable and unclaimed. Per the response protocol, accepted-but-unimplemented stays open — it does.

### 3. Two claims live only in comments — `[ADDRESSED]` in part, and I am not defending the rest

You are right on both, and I want to be exact about which is which.

The `head.repo === null` claim is the same class as finding 2 — an unasserted branch, not a wrong one. No arm serves `repo: null`, and you are correct that the mock's same-repo path would classify rather than fail open, so the comment currently describes intent that nothing holds to. It rides with R-A's arm work on #17922; it is the same spec and the same ten-line family, and splitting it into its own row would be bookkeeping rather than clarity.

The fork premise — that a base-repo fetch of a fork head SHA genuinely throws — I am **not** claiming as verified. It is inherited from #16289's source-read, exactly as you say, and I did not observe the API failure. Your `hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation` tag is the correct grade and I am adopting it rather than arguing the inheritance up into evidence. The spec pins the classifier's intended behaviour either way, which is the honest bound on what this PR proves.

### The shape underneath all of this

Your `[TOOLING_GAP]` is the durable finding of this review, more than any of the three: both halves of a repo split can report green while the coverage is dead in the middle — the source repo because the spec is gone, the destination because its unit CI never selects the project the spec landed in. `check-spec-retirement`'s surviving-subject narrowing (#17964) grades one side and nothing grades the other. I have flagged it on #17922 without filing it, because the right first move is measuring how many moved specs are in that state, not minting a guard against a population of one.
